items.title: Buddy Burns and Frank Pasley Interview, 1968-09-23
items.q: He came down to New Orleans and I left New Orleans and went off with him.

ctx.x: You've probably seen it. It was in a red book. Fake book. Many pictures. Yeah. But it had mostly all the old musicians from New Orleans in it. I can't recall the name of it because a saxophone player, a clinty player named Earl Pearson, he bought the book and he showed it to me. Ray Allen had the book. And that's his cousin, Earl Pearson. And he let me see the picture and I read the article. Well, I had played on the boat in New Orleans. On which one? The JS. Oh, the Dewey Jackson. The Streckwood Line.
Oh, you played in Dewey Jackson's band? Yeah, Dewey Jackson. Out of St. Louis? Yeah.
He came down to New Orleans and I left New Orleans and went off with him.
